# Model card

*Generated by `scripts/make_model_card.py` from `reports/metrics.json` (trained 2026-10-18T08:57:03+00:00).*

## What it does

Predicts the probability that a credit card customer misses next month's payment, from the credit limit and the last six months of bills, payments and repayment status. A policy turns that probability into approve, refer or decline, and anything not approved comes with its reasons.

**Suitable for:** demonstrating an end-to-end, evaluated and audited credit risk model on real data.

**Not suitable for:** real lending decisions. The data is from one Taiwanese lender in 2005, the cost figures behind the decision policy are illustrative, and the model has not been validated on later or other data.

## Data

- UCI *Default of Credit Card Clients* (Yeh, 2009), CC BY 4.0 — see [`DATA.md`](DATA.md)
- 30,000 customers, 35 duplicate records dropped, leaving 29,965
- 22.1% defaulted the following month
- Split 23,972 train / 5,993 test, stratified by outcome. Every choice below was made on the training data; the test set was scored once, at the end.

## How the model was chosen

Cross-validated AUC on the training data (5 folds):

| Model | CV AUC |
|---|---|
| Logistic regression (benchmark) | 0.7557 ± 0.0088 |
| **Gradient boosting, tuned** | **0.7882 ± 0.0081** |

Settings chosen by a randomised search over 40 candidates; early stopping settled on 122 trees.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `l2_regularization` | 0.067 |
| `learning_rate` | 0.0361 |
| `max_features` | 0.6499 |
| `max_leaf_nodes` | 18 |
| `min_samples_leaf` | 147 |

## Results on the held-out test set

| Measure | Model | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| AUC (ranking quality) | **0.7768** | logistic regression 0.7473; coin flip 0.5 |
| KS statistic | 0.4206 | |
| Precision-recall AUC | 0.5538 | random 0.2213 |
| Brier score (lower is better) | 0.1357 | no skill 0.1723 |
| Calibration error | 0.0134 | 0 = probabilities exact |

The test AUC is 0.0114 below the cross-validated estimate. A gap of this size is ordinary variation for a single test set of 5,993; the test figure is the one to quote.

Accuracy is deliberately not a headline: predicting "will repay" for everyone is 77.9% accurate and catches no defaulters.

## Decisions

- **Approve** when the probability of default is below 0.167. Lending to a customer who defaults is set to cost 5x as much as turning away one who would have repaid, and this is where the two balance.
- **Decline** at 0.50 or above: more likely than not to default.
- **Refer** to a person in between.

On the test set:

| | |
|---|---|
| Approved / referred / declined | 56.6% / 31.7% / 11.7% |
| Default rate among approved | **10.4%**, against 22.1% if everyone were approved |
| Defaulters kept from automatic approval | 73.5% (35.7% declined outright) |
| Customers who repaid but were declined | 4.8% |

The cost ratio is illustrative; a lender would set it from its own losses and margins, and the thresholds follow.

## Fairness

The model never sees sex, marital status, age or education. The audit checks outcomes for each anyway. It can test sex, marital status, age; it cannot test race or colour, religion, national origin, receipt of public assistance, which are not in the data. Full explanation in [`FAIRNESS.md`](FAIRNESS.md).

| Group | Approval ratio | Four-fifths rule | Repayment ratio | Amplification | Equal-opportunity gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sex | 0.941 | pass | 0.953 | 0.99 | 0.034 |
| Marital status | 0.995 | pass | 0.954 | 1.04 | 0.020 |
| Age band | 0.902 | pass | 0.948 | 0.95 | 0.062 |
| Education | 0.846 | pass | 0.898 | 0.94 | 0.052 |

Amplification below 1 means approvals are more unequal than actual repayment; above 1, less.

## Limitations

- **One lender, one place, one year.** 2005 Taiwan. Nothing here shows the model would hold up elsewhere or later.
- **No test across time.** All customers come from the same six months, so the evaluation cannot measure drift.
- **Two of the repayment codes are undocumented.** -2 and 0 are the most common values but are not defined by the source; they are used as ordered codes without inventing a meaning.
- **The fairness audit is bounded by the data.** Four protected bases are absent, and some groups are too small to assess.
- **The decision policy's costs are illustrative.**
